messages:
Maria Chen: Follow-up from the streaming retries RFCI want to float a concrete idea: add an explicit session header so short-lived retry/resume attempts can be routed to the same backend and reuse KV/prefix caches. Proposal: header `x-stream-session: <uuid>` (canonical name noted) plus optional resume trailer `x-resume-token` on the final chunk. This should reduce recompute for transient reconnects.

Devon K: does this require idempotency? what about endpoints that mutate state mid-stream?

Maria Chen: we won't use sticky sessions for side-effecting routes. Route config will opt-in/opt-out and the gateway will reject sticky headers for any route marked "non-resumable".

Suraj P: ops concerns: unbounded stickiness = hot shards. we need TTL + lease renewal from backend. also a clear invalidation signal when a backend restarts or loses state (so session binding is not considered valid).

Adam L: fallback approach: if the bound backend is gone and resume token can't be validated, route to a stateless fallback (smaller/fast replica) and return a progress hint to the client instead of forcing a full restart. Less terrible UX.

Lina R: observability ask: emit session-level traces and periodic progress trailers (e.g. `x-progress: 37%`) so the Console can display live progress and cost so we can attribute tokens. Add session lifespan metrics.

Devon K: rough header example for SDK teams: 

```
POST /v1/streams/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.dev
Authorization: Bearer <token>
x-stream-session: 0f8fad5b-d9cb-469f-a165-70867728950e
x-trace-id: 01abc...
```

Backend ends include `Trailer: x-resume-token` and the final trailer `x-resume-token: <opaque>` when resumable.

OpsBot: perf note: sticky sessions will raise per-host CPU/memory under hot keys. Recommend perf sim with 10k synthetic concurrent sessions (sticky-sim) before we flip on any default.

Maria Chen: routing options: 1) consistent-hash(session-id) for placement (good cache locality, rebalance pain), 2) ephemeral map+lease (centralized binding, easier to move but needs coordination), 3) hybrid: CH for initial placement + ephemeral map for overrides after failover. Thoughts?

David H: tradeoffs: CH yields best locality but large cache churn on node changes. map+lease is operationally heavier. hybrid seems pragmatic: CH reduces coordinator load; map for transient overrides and admin detaches.

Suraj P: security: resume tokens must be opaque, tenant-scoped, and cryptographically bound to prevent cross-tenant acceptance. TTL and key rotation required. Also ensure token contains no raw model state.

Lina R: client surface: SDKs should expose a resume(token) call and surface progress events. Also add guidance for header canonicalization (`x-stream-session` lowercase) for nginx/envoy proxies that lowercase headers. Document canonical header name and middleware behavior.

Adam L: tests we need: backend crash mid-session, long-tail churn with varying TTLs, tenant isolation fault injection, perf under 1k/10k/50k sticky sessions, admin invalidate behavior.

Maria Chen: next steps: I'll draft an RFC covering header schema, lifecycle (TTL/lease/renewal), routing algorithms, fallback semantics, observability, security model, admin APIs, and rollout plan. Volunteers to review?

Devon K: will review.

Suraj P: I'll own ops/runbook + chaos tests.

Lina R: I'll write observability, Console UI hooks, and SDK samples.

David H: I'll run perf sims and routing perf writeup.

Adam L: I'll document fallback UX and client guidance.

Maria Chen: Admin API question: should we expose `POST /admin/sessions/{id}/invalidate` to force-detach a sticky session? Useful for debugging and incident mitigation.

Adam L: yes, ops-only with audit logs.

OpsBot: task created: perf job `sticky-sim-v1` in perf infra.

Lina R: small nit: prefer we document header in lowercase in proxy configs (`x-stream-session`) and call out canonicalization rules.

Maria Chen: good call. RFC will include canonical header name, sample proxy snippets, and migration plan (opt-in routes first, telemetry gated). Co-authors welcome.

Devon K: thanks all, excited to see the RFC.

Suraj P: +1
